definition: Monitoring or auditing creates evidence about conduct so compliance can be assessed.
A detected deviation triggers a material or social cost for the actor.
An advance pledge or contract makes deviation costly or constrains later choices.
Past behavior is aggregated or shared to shape future treatment and incentives.
Collectively recognized norms or governance rules coordinate or constrain conduct.
Rewards or transfers depend on contributions, compliance, or others conduct.
Agents deny access or change partners in response to conduct.
A system limits available actions or access to protect shared interests.
An independent adjudicator decides contested conduct, appeals, or remedies.
An agent cooperates, reciprocates, or withholds cooperation based on others behavior.
